news.headline: PM orders increase in country's strategic petroleum reserves; Cabinet Committee on Energy approves changes to Oil Refining Policy 2023
news.summary: Published/updated Jul 28, 2026 1:36pm PKT: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, chairing a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Energy at the PM's House, approved amendments to the 'Pakistan Oil Refining Policy for Upgradation of Existing Brownfield Refineries 2023' - requiring production of environment-friendly Euro-V-standard fuel, reduction of furnace oil and low-quality petroleum products output, and compliance with international environmental commitments. The amendments aim to unlock nearly $6 billion in investment across Pakistan's five existing refineries (combined capacity approx. 449,400 bpd, currently operating at less than half that level) - a follow-through on the Petroleum Division's amendments to the same Brownfield Refining Policy first reported 2026-07-13 (already logged this newslog at impact 4). PM Shehbaz directed authorities to promote the revised policy among Gulf investors via roadshows in Qatar, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states to attract investment in brownfield refinery upgrade projects, and ordered reforms to the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). No individual refinery (ATRL, NRL, PRL, PARCO, Cnergyico) named specifically in this article; tagged to the universe's core-tier refiners (ATRL, NRL, PRL) as the direct beneficiaries of a sector-wide brownfield-refining policy. Logged as impact 4 (regulatory action) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10); escalation flagged.

No EPS or dividend figure disclosed in the source reviewed. Logged as impact 3 (notable results) for this small-weight, listed-tier universe constituent.

news.headline: Honda Atlas Cars (HCAR) Q4FY26 profit triples to Rs2.49bn on 41% sales growth, Rs1.59bn Sindh SIDC settlement gain
news.summary: Published Jul 29, 2026 1:01pm PKT: Honda Atlas Cars (Pakistan) Limited (PSX: HCAR) reported net profit of Rs2.49bn for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, up threefold from Rs828.44m in the same quarter last year; EPS tripled to Rs17.41 from Rs5.80. Sales rose 41% YoY to Rs37.20bn from Rs26.46bn; other income surged 3.8x YoY to Rs2.09bn. Units sold jumped 43% YoY to 7,918 (vs 5,520 prior year); a Rs1.59bn one-off gain from a settlement agreement with the Government of Sindh regarding an SIDC liability was a major contributor to the profit surge alongside the higher unit sales. No dividend disclosed in the source reviewed. Logged as impact 4 (material earnings surprise) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10) given the magnitude of the profit/EPS beat, noting a meaningful portion is a non-recurring settlement gain; escalation flagged.

news.headline: KSE-100 confirmed Wednesday close: index falls 1,580.90 points (-0.89%) as fresh US/Saudi strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq jolt oil markets

A sharp single-session commodity move (Brent/WTI both +~3%) per desk news-impact criteria (Rule 10), bearing on Pakistan's E&P names (OGDC, PPL, MARI), refiners (ATRL, NRL, PRL) and HUBC among index heavyweights, plus renewed inflation/import-bill pressure economy-wide. Logged as impact 4; escalation flagged.

news.headline: PPL discovers new oil and gas reserves in Sindh - fourth consecutive discovery in Shah Bandar Block (Rahi X-1 well)
news.summary: Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PSX: PPL) announced a new hydrocarbon discovery at the Rahi X-1 exploratory well in the Shah Bandar Exploration License, Sujawal district, Sindh - the fourth consecutive discovery in the block, following Benari X-1 (Dec 2018), Jhim East X-1 (2023) and Pateji X-1 (Nov 2024). Production testing yielded 12 barrels of oil per day (bopd) and 0.493 million standard cubic feet of gas per day (mmscfd) at a 32/64-inch choke. PPL is operator with 63% working interest; Mari Energies Limited (PSX: MARI) holds the remaining 32% participating interest. Per brokerage estimates cited in the article, the discovery could add approximately Rs0.036/share annually to PPL's earnings and approximately Rs0.042/share to Mari Energies' earnings, based on the tested production rate - a modest absolute production volume. Logged as impact 3 (notable company/sector news) for both PPL and MARI.

news.summary: State Bank of Pakistan-held foreign exchange reserves fell $229 million over the week to $17.03bn, down from $17.259bn a week earlier (week ended July 24, 2026). Routine weekly reserves data, consistent in kind with prior weekly reserve items already logged this newslog; logged as impact 2 (minor/background).
